# google\-deepmind/alphafoldsparkPowered by Gemini

# google\-deepmind/alphafoldsparkPowered by Gemini

Updated onJul 20, 2026Commit[`c77e5d2`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/tree/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6)Gemini can make mistakes, so double\-check it\.![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

This repository provides the AlphaFold system, which predicts the three\-dimensional structures of proteins\. It transforms raw protein sequences into accurate structural models by integrating advanced machine learning with biophysical principles, orchestrating data acquisition, model inference, and structural refinement\.

 The system's operation involves several distinct stages:

 - **Installation and Deployment**: This stage covers setting up the AlphaFold environment and acquiring the necessary biological databases\. It frequently utilizes Docker to ensure a consistent and reproducible setup, managing dependencies and data required for predictions\. Further details are available in [AlphaFold Installation and Deployment](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-installation-and-deployment)\.
- **Inference Pipeline**: This is the core of AlphaFold, processing raw protein sequences into model\-ready features, executing the neural network models, and generating initial structure predictions\. It involves sophisticated data input processing, feature generation \(such as Multiple Sequence Alignments and structural templates\), and the execution of the deep learning architecture\. See [AlphaFold Inference Pipeline](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-inference-pipeline) for more information\.
- **Protein Structure Refinement and Analysis**: After an initial prediction, this stage refines the predicted structures to improve accuracy and resolve structural inconsistencies\. This typically includes energy minimization using methods like Amber relaxation and applies advanced 3D geometric transformations for precise structural manipulation\. Consult [Protein Structure Refinement and Analysis](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#protein-structure-refinement-and-analysis) for specifics\.
- **Data Management and External Tool Integration**: AlphaFold relies on large biological databases and integrates with various third\-party bioinformatics tools to generate input features\. This component manages access to databases like the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database and provides wrappers for tools such as [run\_alphafold\.py L79](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/run_alphafold.py#L79) and [jackhmmer\.py L31](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L31)\. [AlphaFold Data Management and External Tool Integration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-data-management-and-external-tool-integration) offers additional context\.
- **AlphaFold Server Job Submission**: This capability allows for the automated submission and management of protein structure prediction tasks to an AlphaFold server\. It defines a standardized JSON format for specifying jobs, including molecular entities, sequences, and modeling parameters, enabling scalable and reproducible predictions\. Learn more in [AlphaFold Server Job Submission](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-server-job-submission)\.## AlphaFold Installation and Deployment

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

To deploy AlphaFold for protein structure prediction, two main components are required: the AlphaFold application itself and the extensive biological databases it utilizes\. The process involves setting up the environment, acquiring the necessary data, and running the prediction pipeline, often facilitated by containerization for reproducibility\.

 The AlphaFold application's core implementation resides in the [`(root)`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/) directory\. This includes the pipeline for processing protein features, executing models, and refining predictions\. The version of the AlphaFold project is defined in [`alphafold/version.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/version.py)\. The primary script for orchestrating predictions is [`run_alphafold.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/run_alphafold.py), which integrates feature generation, model execution, confidence scoring, and optional structural relaxation\.

 A consistent and reproducible deployment environment for AlphaFold is achieved through Docker\. The [`docker`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/docker) directory contains the necessary components for containerized execution\. The [README\.md?plain=1 L106](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L106) \([`docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/docker/Dockerfile)\) outlines the environment setup, including system dependencies, external bioinformatics tools such as [README\.md?plain=1 L733](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L733) and [kalign\.py L36](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/kalign.py#L36), and the Python environment with GPU support\. The [README\.md?plain=1 L119](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L119) script \([`docker/run_docker.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/docker/run_docker.py)\) orchestrates the Docker container execution, handling mounts for input data, databases, and output directories, as well as configuring GPU access and passing prediction parameters\. For more details on this aspect, refer to [Dockerized Deployment and Execution](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-installation-and-deployment-dockerized-deployment-and-execution)\.

 AlphaFold relies on several large biological databases and model parameters\. The acquisition and management of this data are automated through a collection of shell scripts located in the [`scripts`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts) directory\. The [README\.md?plain=1 L69](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L69) script \([`scripts/download_all_data.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts/download_all_data.sh)\) acts as an orchestrator, calling individual scripts to download AlphaFold model parameters \([`scripts/download_alphafold_params.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts/download_alphafold_params.sh)\) and various genetic databases like BFD, MGnify, PDB70, PDB mmCIF, PDB SeqRes, UniRef30, UniRef90, and UniProt\. These scripts ensure that all necessary data is downloaded, extracted, and organized in the specified data directory\. Further details on this process can be found in [AlphaFold Data Acquisition and Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-installation-and-deployment-alphafold-data-acquisition-and-management)\.

 Once the application is set up and the data is acquired, predictions can be initiated by providing FASTA sequences\. The AlphaFold pipeline then generates input features, runs the models, calculates confidence scores like predicted Local Distance Difference Test \(pLDDT\) and Predicted Aligned Error \(PAE\), and outputs the predicted protein structures in PDB and mmCIF formats\. The outputs also include debug and timing information\. Users can choose between different model presets \(e\.g\., monomer, multimer\) and database presets \(full or reduced databases\) to balance accuracy and computational resources\. The contribution guidelines for modifying the AlphaFold codebase, including bug fixes and documentation, are provided in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/CONTRIBUTING.md)\.### Dockerized Deployment and Execution

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

AlphaFold's deployment and execution within a containerized environment is managed through Docker\. This approach ensures consistent and reproducible protein structure predictions\. The Docker setup involves a [README\.md?plain=1 L106](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L106) for environment configuration, dependency installation, and GPU support, coupled with a Python script that orchestrates container execution, including data mounts and argument passing\.

 The Docker image is defined by the [`docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/docker/Dockerfile)\. This file details the steps for building a robust Docker image, starting from an [README\.md?plain=1 L88](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L88) base to enable GPU acceleration\. It handles the installation of system dependencies, compiles bioinformatics tools like [README\.md?plain=1 L732](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L732) from source, and sets up a Miniconda environment for Python\. Key steps include copying the AlphaFold application code, installing Python dependencies \(including specific [README\.md?plain=1 L735](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L735) and [Dockerfile L72](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/docker/Dockerfile#L72) versions with CUDA support\), and configuring necessary library paths\. A custom entrypoint script, [Dockerfile L89](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/docker/Dockerfile#L89), is created to address GPU visibility issues on Debian\-based images before launching the main AlphaFold Python script\.

 The execution of AlphaFold within this Docker container is managed by [`docker/run_docker.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/docker/run_docker.py)\. This Python script parses command\-line flags to control various AlphaFold parameters, such as GPU usage, input FASTA paths, output directories, and database presets\. It programmatically constructs absolute paths for necessary database files and input data\. The script then generates Docker mount objects to bind host directories and files into the container, making data accessible to AlphaFold\. It initializes a Docker client, configures GPU access, and executes the AlphaFold container, passing configured arguments and setting environment variables for GPU memory optimization\. The script also includes signal handling to gracefully terminate the container upon interruption and streams container output for monitoring\. The Python dependencies for this orchestration script are defined in [`docker/requirements.txt`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/docker/requirements.txt), which pins [pyproject\.toml L40](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/pyproject.toml#L40) and [README\.md?plain=1 L47](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L47) to specific versions for consistent operation\.### AlphaFold Data Acquisition and Management

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The AlphaFold system relies on a comprehensive collection of biological databases and model parameters for accurate protein structure prediction\. These necessary data are acquired and organized through a set of automated scripts located in the [`scripts`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts) directory\. This modular approach ensures that various data types, each with its specific download and processing requirements, are handled systematically\.

 The central orchestration of the data download process is managed by the [`scripts/download_all_data.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts/download_all_data.sh) script\. This script acts as a master controller, validating arguments and essential dependencies like [README\.md?plain=1 L64](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L64) and [README\.md?plain=1 L67](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L67), then sequentially invoking specialized sub\-scripts for each database\. This modular design allows for efficient management and selective execution of data downloads, supporting both full and reduced database modes\. For instance, depending on the chosen mode, it might download the entire BFD database via [`scripts/download_bfd.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts/download_bfd.sh) or a smaller version using [`scripts/download_small_bfd.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts/download_small_bfd.sh)\.

 Beyond database acquisition, the system also requires AlphaFold's trained model parameters\. These are downloaded and extracted by the [`scripts/download_alphafold_params.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts/download_alphafold_params.sh) script from a Google Cloud Storage URL, ensuring the prediction models are up\-to\-date\.

 Other scripts in this directory are dedicated to acquiring specific databases:

 - [`scripts/download_mgnify.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts/download_mgnify.sh) handles the MGnify database\.
- [`scripts/download_pdb70.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts/download_pdb70.sh) manages the PDB70 database\.
- [`scripts/download_pdb_mmcif.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts/download_pdb_mmcif.sh) downloads, decompresses, and flattens Protein Data Bank \(PDB\) mmCIF files, including an [README\.md?plain=1 L226](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L226) file for outdated entries\.
- [`scripts/download_pdb_seqres.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts/download_pdb_seqres.sh) retrieves the PDB Sequence Residue database and filters it to retain only protein sequences\.
- [`scripts/download_uniref30.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts/download_uniref30.sh) and [`scripts/download_uniref90.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts/download_uniref90.sh) download and extract the UniRef30 and UniRef90 databases, respectively\.
- [`scripts/download_uniprot.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/scripts/download_uniprot.sh) downloads, unzips, and merges SwissProt and TrEMBL databases, which are essential for AlphaFold\-Multimer\.

 These scripts consistently incorporate robust error handling, using [requirements\.txt L12](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/requirements.txt#L12) to ensure immediate exit upon command failure, thereby preventing incomplete or corrupted data installations\. The use of [README\.md?plain=1 L64](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L64) and [README\.md?plain=1 L67](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L67) further enhances download efficiency and reliability\.## AlphaFold Inference Pipeline

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The AlphaFold v2\.0 inference pipeline processes raw protein sequence data to predict 3D protein structures\. This process begins by transforming raw sequences into a feature set that the neural network can interpret, proceeds through the core model execution where the structure is iteratively predicted, and concludes with the generation of confidence metrics and a final structural representation\.

 The pipeline's common components, defined in the [`alphafold/common`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/common) directory, include data structures for managing protein information, methods for calculating confidence metrics, and constants related to amino acid residues\. For instance, the [protein\.py L65](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/common/protein.py#L65) dataclass in [`alphafold/common/protein.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/common/protein.py) encapsulates atom positions, amino acid types, and residue indices, and includes functionality for converting between internal representations and standard PDB or mmCIF formats\. Confidence scores like pLDDT \(predicted Local Distance Difference Test\) and PAE \(predicted aligned error\) are computed and serialized by functions in [`alphafold/common/confidence.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/common/confidence.py)\. These metrics provide quantitative assessments of the accuracy of the predicted structures\. Additionally, [`alphafold/common/residue_constants.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/common/residue_constants.py) contains biochemical constants for amino acids, such as chi angle definitions and atom positions within rigid groups, which are foundational for structural computations\. When generating final mmCIF outputs, AlphaFold\-specific metadata, including licensing, authorship, and model quality metrics, is added via [`alphafold/common/mmcif_metadata.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/common/mmcif_metadata.py) to ensure proper attribution and data sharing\.

 The process of preparing data for the AlphaFold model, including feature generation and handling multiple sequence alignments \(MSAs\), is detailed in [AlphaFold Data Input and Feature Generation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-inference-pipeline-alphafold-data-input-and-feature-generation)\. Once features are prepared, the core AlphaFold model architecture and execution, including the Evoformer and iterative refinement steps, are responsible for generating initial structural predictions\. This is further elaborated in [AlphaFold Model Architecture and Execution](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-inference-pipeline-alphafold-model-architecture-and-execution)\. After an initial prediction, the structures undergo a refinement process, often involving Amber relaxation, to improve accuracy and resolve any structural issues, as described in [Protein Structure Refinement and Analysis](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#protein-structure-refinement-and-analysis)\.### AlphaFold Data Input and Feature Generation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The AlphaFold inference pipeline begins by transforming raw protein sequences into a comprehensive set of features that the neural network model can consume\. This process involves parsing various biological data formats, generating Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\), identifying and featurizing structural templates, and orchestrating these steps for both single\-chain \(monomer\) and multi\-chain \(multimer\) predictions\.

 The [pipeline\.py L123](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/pipeline.py#L123) classes in [`alphafold/data/pipeline.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/pipeline.py) and [`alphafold/data/pipeline_multimer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/pipeline_multimer.py) are responsible for orchestrating feature generation\. For both monomers and multimers, the process starts by accepting protein sequences, typically in FASTA format\. These sequences are first converted into basic sequence\-level features such as amino acid types and residue indices\.

 A crucial step in feature generation is creating MSAs, which represent evolutionary information\. This involves running external bioinformatics tools like Jackhmmer and HHblits against large protein sequence databases\. These tools search for homologous sequences and align them, providing rich evolutionary context for each residue in the target protein\. The output of these tools, often in formats like Stockholm or A3M, is then parsed and consolidated into a unified MSA feature set\. The directory [`alphafold/data/tools`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools) contains Python wrappers for these external tools, handling their execution, temporary file management, and output parsing\. For more details on how these external tools are integrated, see [External Bioinformatics Tool Wrappers](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-data-management-and-external-tool-integration-external-bioinformatics-tool-wrappers)\.

 Simultaneously, the pipeline searches for known protein structures that are similar to the target sequence, using tools like HHsearch or HMMsearch\. These "template hits" provide valuable structural information that can guide the prediction process\. Once identified, these template hits are processed to extract relevant structural features, including atomic coordinates and their masks\. This featurization involves parsing mmCIF files \([`alphafold/data/mmcif_parsing.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/mmcif_parsing.py)\), aligning template sequences to the query, and ensuring the structural integrity of the templates\. The featurization process also includes pre\-filtering steps based on criteria such as template release dates and sequence similarity to ensure only high\-quality templates are used\.

 For multimer predictions, the process introduces additional complexities\. Each chain in a multimeric complex is initially processed to generate its individual features\. Then, a sophisticated MSA pairing logic is applied, particularly within [`alphafold/data/msa_pairing.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/msa_pairing.py) and [`alphafold/data/feature_processing.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/feature_processing.py)\. This step aims to identify and align homologous sequences across different protein chains within the complex, which is critical for modeling inter\-chain interactions\. Chains are grouped by sequence to identify homomers \(identical subunits\), and unique identifiers \([example\.json L34](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/example.json#L34), [msa\_pairing\.py L54](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/msa_pairing.py#L54), [model\.py L49](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/model.py#L49)\) are assigned to residues to distinguish between different chains and their symmetry relationships\. After pairing, the features from all chains are merged and cropped to manage computational resources, resulting in a single feature dictionary that represents the entire multimeric complex\.

 Throughout this entire process, various biological file formats are parsed by [`alphafold/data/parsers.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/parsers.py) to extract the necessary information\. This includes parsing FASTA for sequences, Stockholm and A3M for MSAs, HHR for template search results, and mmCIF for detailed structural data\. The parsing modules provide structured data representations such as [parsers\.py L30](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/parsers.py#L30) for multiple sequence alignments and [parsers\.py L62](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/parsers.py#L62) for template search results, which are then used in downstream featurization steps\.### AlphaFold Model Architecture and Execution

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The AlphaFold model architecture processes protein features and iteratively refines a protein's predicted 3D structure\. The core neural network functionality is orchestrated by [modules\.py L289](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/modules.py#L289) modules, defined in [`alphafold/model/modules.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/modules.py) for monomer prediction and [`alphafold/model/modules_multimer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/modules_multimer.py) for multimer prediction\. These modules coordinate iterative prediction steps \([modules\.py L134](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/modules.py#L134)\) and manage the overall flow from initial feature embedding through to final structure prediction\.

 The [modules\.py L134](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/modules.py#L134) is a single pass through the network, consisting of an [config\.py L857](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/config.py#L857) component and a [folding\.py L465](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/folding.py#L465)\. The [config\.py L857](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/config.py#L857) handles the initial embedding of input features and subsequent processing through the Evoformer stack\. Within the Evoformer, a key component is the [modules\.py L1751](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/modules.py#L1751), which refines sequence and multiple sequence alignment \(MSA\) representations using various attention mechanisms, such as [folding\.py L37](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/folding.py#L37), [modules\.py L858](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/modules.py#L858), and [config\.py L763](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/config.py#L763)\.

 The [folding\.py L465](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/folding.py#L465) \(defined in [`alphafold/model/folding.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/folding.py) for monomer and [`alphafold/model/folding_multimer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/folding_multimer.py) for multimer\) takes the Evoformer's outputs and iteratively refines residue positions and orientations\. This involves [folding\.py L37](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/folding.py#L37) for geometry\-aware attention, [folding\.py L290](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/folding.py#L290) to update hidden representations and affine transformations, and [folding\.py L989](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/folding.py#L989) to predict side\-chain atom positions\. The output of the [folding\.py L465](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/folding.py#L465) is a trajectory of residue [modules\.py L1244](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/modules.py#L1244) transformations and sidechain predictions, which are then converted into full atom positions\.

 The model's execution is managed by the [model\.py L72](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/model.py#L72) class in [`alphafold/model/model.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/model.py)\. This class loads pre\-trained parameters \(via [`alphafold/model/data.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/data.py)\), processes input features using [model\.py L139](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/model.py#L139), and executes the model's forward pass\. After the initial structure prediction, [model\.py L72](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/model.py#L72) also calculates confidence metrics like predicted Local Distance Difference Test \(pLDDT\) and Predicted TM\-score \(pTM\), which are crucial for assessing prediction quality\.

 Model configurations are managed by [`alphafold/model/config.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/config.py), which defines base settings for monomer and multimer models and applies specific modifications through [config\.py L55](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/config.py#L55) and [config\.py L30](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/config.py#L30)\. The [base\_config\.py L132](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/base_config.py#L132) class in [`alphafold/model/base_config.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/base_config.py) provides a framework for creating hierarchical, type\-annotated configurations that can be frozen to prevent accidental modification, ensuring reproducibility\.

 Geometric operations are fundamental to the [folding\.py L465](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/folding.py#L465) and are handled by the [`alphafold/model/geometry`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry) directory\. This includes [vector\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/vector.py#L33) for vectors, [rotation\_matrix\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L33) for rotation matrices, and [rigid\_matrix\_vector\.py L32](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L32) for rigid transformations, all designed for efficient, batched computations with JAX\. The [lddt\.py L19](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/lddt.py#L19) function in [`alphafold/model/lddt.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/lddt.py) computes an approximate lDDT score to compare predicted and true structures based on distance matrices\.

 The [layer\_stack\.py L212](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/layer_stack.py#L212) utility in [`alphafold/model/layer_stack.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/layer_stack.py) provides a mechanism for stacking multiple instances of a Haiku function, allowing each instance to have independent parameters\. This enables the creation of deep neural networks or iterative processes with non\-shared weights\. For large inputs, sharded computation utilities in [`alphafold/model/mapping.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/mapping.py) allow processing in smaller chunks, managing memory trade\-offs\.### Common Data Structures and Confidence Metrics

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The AlphaFold pipeline utilizes a set of foundational data structures and constants to represent and manipulate protein information, alongside utilities for assessing prediction confidence\. The core data structure for managing protein geometries is the [protein\.py L65](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/common/protein.py#L65) dataclass, defined in [`alphafold/common/protein.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/common/protein.py)\. This dataclass encapsulates critical structural data such as atom positions, amino acid types, atom masks, residue and chain indices, and B\-factors\. It includes utilities for parsing standard protein formats like PDB and mmCIF strings, as well as for serializing internal [protein\.py L65](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/common/protein.py#L65) objects back into these formats\. This allows for seamless integration with existing bioinformatics tools and databases\.

 Residue\-specific biochemical constants and properties are centralized in [`alphafold/common/residue_constants.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/common/residue_constants.py)\. This module provides detailed information crucial for structural modeling, including definitions for torsion \(chi\) angles, relative atom positions within rigid groups, and mappings between various residue and atom naming conventions\. It also includes functions for operations such as one\-hot encoding of amino acid sequences, which is a common requirement for machine learning models\. The constants defined here ensure consistency and accuracy in structural calculations throughout the AlphaFold system\.

 To evaluate the quality and reliability of predicted protein structures, AlphaFold incorporates functions for calculating key confidence metrics\. The [`alphafold/common/confidence.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/common/confidence.py) module is dedicated to computing and formatting these metrics\. It generates per\-residue Predicted Local Distance Difference Test \(pLDDT\) scores, which indicate the confidence of each residue's predicted position\. It also calculates the Predicted Aligned Error \(PAE\), providing a measure of global accuracy and relative positional error between residue pairs\. Additionally, this module computes predicted TM\-scores, which evaluate the topological similarity between predicted and \(hypothetical\) true structures\. These metrics are formatted into JSON outputs, facilitating their use in downstream analyses and visualizations\. Furthermore, to ensure proper attribution and standardized data sharing, AlphaFold\-specific metadata, including licensing, authorship, citation details, and model quality metrics like global pLDDT, are embedded into mmCIF files using the functionality in [`alphafold/common/mmcif_metadata.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/common/mmcif_metadata.py)\. This process enriches the structural data with important contextual information\.## Protein Structure Refinement and Analysis

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Post\-prediction, AlphaFold refines protein structures using Amber relaxation to enhance accuracy and resolve issues\. This process addresses structural inconsistencies, minimizes energy, and ensures the biological relevance of predicted structures\. It also incorporates a suite of tools for advanced geometric transformations, which are fundamental to protein modeling\.

 This refinement process is primarily handled by the [README\.md?plain=1 L593](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L593) module, found at [`alphafold/relax`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax)\. The module's [relax\.py L23](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax/relax.py#L23) class provides an interface for configuring and executing the relaxation pipeline\. This pipeline leverages OpenMM for energy minimization, applying harmonic restraints to guide the structure towards a stable conformation\. During this iterative process, the system actively identifies and addresses structural violations, such as clashes, by progressively relaxing restraints in problematic regions\. Protein input and output are managed using PDB strings and [run\_alphafold\.py L302](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/run_alphafold.py#L302) objects, and utilities are provided to handle B\-factor data and validate atom types\. More details on this process can be found in [Amber Relaxation and Energy Minimization](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#protein-structure-refinement-and-analysis-amber-relaxation-and-energy-minimization)\.

 Complementing the structural refinement, AlphaFold includes a [README\.md?plain=1 L369](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L369) module at [`alphafold/model/geometry`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry) that provides foundational 3D geometric operations\. This module defines specialized classes for vectors \([vector\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/vector.py#L33)\), rotation matrices \([rotation\_matrix\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L33)\), and rigid transformations \([rigid\_matrix\_vector\.py L32](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L32)\)\. These structures support batched operations and are compatible with JAX for efficient, high\-performance computations\. They facilitate tasks such as composing transformations, applying rotations to points, and calculating distances and angles, all critical for accurate protein structure manipulation and analysis\. The detailed implementation of these structures and operations is discussed in [3D Geometric Transformations and Data Structures](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#protein-structure-refinement-and-analysis-3d-geometric-transformations-and-data-structures)\.### Amber Relaxation and Energy Minimization

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The AlphaFold pipeline incorporates Amber relaxation to refine predicted protein structures, addressing structural issues and improving accuracy\. This iterative process uses OpenMM for energy minimization, harmonic restraints to maintain structural integrity, and identifies and resolves structural violations\.

 The relaxation process begins by cleaning up input protein structures using a combination of [pyproject\.toml L49](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/pyproject.toml#L49) and custom logic in [`alphafold/relax/cleanup.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax/cleanup.py)\. This step handles issues such as nonstandard residues, heterogens, and missing atoms, ensuring the structure is suitable for energy minimization\. The [cleanup\_test\.py L51](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax/cleanup_test.py#L51) function applies standard [pyproject\.toml L49](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/pyproject.toml#L49) operations, while [amber\_minimize\.py L182](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax/amber_minimize.py#L182) performs specialized fixes like correcting Selenium in Methionine residues\.

 The core of the relaxation is managed by the functions within [`alphafold/relax/amber_minimize.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax/amber_minimize.py)\. It orchestrates an iterative pipeline where an input protein undergoes multiple rounds of energy minimization via [amber\_minimize\.py L446](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax/amber_minimize.py#L446)\. During each round, [amber\_minimize\.py L79](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax/amber_minimize.py#L79) configures OpenMM with an Amber force field and applies harmonic restraints to specific atoms using [amber\_minimize\.py L49](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax/amber_minimize.py#L49) to prevent excessive deviation from the initial structure\. The strength of these restraints is controlled by a [run\_alphafold\.py L691](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/run_alphafold.py#L691) parameter\.

 Following minimization, the structure is analyzed for violations, such as clashes or improbable bond lengths, using the [amber\_minimize\.py L333](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax/amber_minimize.py#L333) function in [`alphafold/relax/amber_minimize.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax/amber_minimize.py)\. Residues involved in these violations are identified and subsequently excluded from restraints in future minimization steps within the current iteration\. This adaptive approach allows problematic regions of the protein to relax more freely, improving the overall quality of the structure while maintaining the integrity of well\-folded regions\. The relaxation process continues until a specified tolerance is met or a maximum number of iterations is reached\.

 The [relax\.py L23](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax/relax.py#L23) class in [`alphafold/relax/relax.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax/relax.py) provides the primary interface for this process\. It takes a protein structure, executes the Amber minimization pipeline via its [relax\.py L60](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/relax/relax.py#L60) method, and returns the refined structure along with debugging information, including energy changes and RMSD\. This ensures that the final predicted protein structures are chemically plausible and physically realistic\.### 3D Geometric Transformations and Data Structures

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The AlphaFold inference pipeline uses a set of foundational 3D geometric operations and data structures to efficiently represent and manipulate protein structures\. These structures are designed for batched computations and JAX compatibility, supporting operations essential for predicting protein tertiary and quaternary structures\.

 The core geometric primitives include:

 - **[vector\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/vector.py#L33) for Vectors:** Represented by the class in [`alphafold/model/geometry/vector.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/vector.py), [vector\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/vector.py#L33) handles 3D vectors\. This class supports common vector arithmetic such as addition, subtraction, scalar multiplication, dot products, and cross products\. It also provides functionality for calculating vector norms, normalizing vectors, and determining dihedral angles between sets of four points\. The implementation utilizes a "Struct of Arrays" \(SoA\) approach for performance with JAX, storing [vector\.py L45](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/vector.py#L45), [vector\.py L46](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/vector.py#L46), and [vector\.py L47](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/vector.py#L47) components as separate arrays\.
- **[rotation\_matrix\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L33) for Rotation Matrices:** Defined in [`alphafold/model/geometry/rotation_matrix.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/rotation_matrix.py), [rotation\_matrix\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L33) encapsulates 3x3 rotation matrices\. It offers methods for inverting rotations \(transposing the matrix\), applying rotations to points, and composing rotations\. The class also includes various constructors to create rotation matrices from different representations, such as two vectors or quaternions\. Like [vector\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/vector.py#L33), it uses an SoA pattern, storing each element of the 3x3 matrix individually for JAX efficiency\.
- **[rigid\_matrix\_vector\.py L32](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L32) for Rigid Transformations:** The [`alphafold/model/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py) file introduces [rigid\_matrix\_vector\.py L32](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L32), which combines a [rotation\_matrix\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L33) \(rotation\) and a [vector\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/vector.py#L33) \(translation\) to represent a 3D rigid transformation\. This class enables operations such as composing transformations, computing inverse transformations, and applying transformations to 3D points\. It supports constructing transformations from 4x4 homogeneous matrices, providing a flexible interface for manipulating protein coordinates\.

 These geometric data structures are enhanced for JAX compatibility through the [struct\_of\_array\.py L191](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/struct_of_array.py#L191) decorator, found in [`alphafold/model/geometry/struct_of_array.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/struct_of_array.py)\. This decorator transforms standard Python dataclasses into JAX\-compatible PyTrees, enabling efficient use with JAX's automatic differentiation and parallel computation capabilities\. This allows these geometric objects to behave like structured arrays, facilitating seamless integration with the larger AlphaFold computational graph\.

 The overall organization in the [`alphafold/model/geometry`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry) directory centralizes these geometric utilities, simplifying their import and use across the codebase\. For testing these geometric calculations, a set of utility functions is provided in [`alphafold/model/geometry/test_utils.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/geometry/test_utils.py), allowing for precise validation of rotation matrices, vectors, and rigid transformations\.## AlphaFold Data Management and External Tool Integration

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

AlphaFold's operation relies on extensive biological databases and the integration of various bioinformatics tools for feature generation\. The system manages access to the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database and orchestrates the use of external tools through Python wrappers\.

 The AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, documented in [`afdb/README.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md), provides a vast collection of predicted protein structures\. This database is hosted on Google Cloud Public Datasets and is accessible through several methods\. Users can perform bulk downloads of the entire dataset or obtain specific subsets\. For targeted data retrieval, metadata querying via BigQuery allows for filtering based on criteria like organism or confidence scores, enabling the creation of custom download manifests\. Each protein entry typically includes atomic coordinates in CIF format and confidence metrics such as pLDDT and Predicted Aligned Error \(PAE\)\. [AlphaFold Protein Structure Database Access and Querying](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-data-management-and-external-tool-integration-alphafold-protein-structure-database-access-and-querying) provides additional details on accessing this resource\.

 To prepare input features for its models, AlphaFold integrates with several third\-party bioinformatics tools\. This integration is handled by Python wrappers located in [`alphafold/data/tools`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools)\. These wrappers manage the execution of command\-line tools like [run\_alphafold\.py L79](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/run_alphafold.py#L79), [run\_alphafold\.py L84](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/run_alphafold.py#L84), [jackhmmer\.py L31](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L31), [hmmbuild\.py L27](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hmmbuild.py#L27), [hmmsearch\.py L29](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L29), and [kalign\.py L36](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/kalign.py#L36)\. The wrappers abstract the complexities of subprocess management, temporary file handling, and output parsing, providing a standardized interface for the AlphaFold pipeline\. For instance, [hhblits\.py L32](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hhblits.py#L32) \([`alphafold/data/tools/hhblits.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hhblits.py)\) performs protein sequence database searches to generate multiple sequence alignments \(MSAs\), while [jackhmmer\.py L31](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L31) \([`alphafold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py)\) facilitates homology searches, with support for streamed database queries to manage large datasets efficiently\. Similarly, [kalign\.py L36](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/kalign.py#L36) \([`alphafold/data/tools/kalign.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/kalign.py)\) is used for multiple sequence alignment\. Utility functions within this directory, such as [utils\.py L25](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/utils.py#L25) \([`alphafold/data/tools/utils.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/utils.py)\), ensure proper cleanup of temporary files and directories generated during tool execution\. Further details on these wrappers can be found in [External Bioinformatics Tool Wrappers](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-data-management-and-external-tool-integration-external-bioinformatics-tool-wrappers)\.### AlphaFold Protein Structure Database Access and Querying

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, hosted on Google Cloud Public Datasets, contains a vast collection of protein structure predictions\. Access methods include bulk downloads of the entire dataset or specific subsets\. The database is organized into sharded [README\.md?plain=1 L250](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L250) files \(e\.g\., [README\.md?plain=1 L88](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L88)\) to optimize download performance by reducing latency associated with numerous small files, as detailed in [`afdb/README.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md)\.

 For bulk retrieval, users can employ [README\.md?plain=1 L178](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L178) with recursive copy operations\. Each protein entry within the database includes a [README\.md?plain=1 L70](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L70) file for atomic coordinates and metadata, a [README\.md?plain=1 L74](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L74) file providing per\-residue [README\.md?plain=1 L369](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L369) confidence metrics, and a [README\.md?plain=1 L79](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L79) file containing [README\.md?plain=1 L258](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L258) confidence metrics\. Auxiliary files such as [README\.md?plain=1 L92](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L92) and [README\.md?plain=1 L100](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L100) are also available\.

 To facilitate custom subset creation and advanced data filtering, the database offers a metadata table \([README\.md?plain=1 L271](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L271)\) accessible via Google Cloud's BigQuery\. This allows users to query fields such as [README\.md?plain=1 L312](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L312), [README\.md?plain=1 L302](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L302), [README\.md?plain=1 L276](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L276), [README\.md?plain=1 L319](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L319), and [README\.md?plain=1 L275](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L275) to generate manifest files for targeted downloads, as described in [`afdb/README.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md)\. This capability enables researchers to retrieve only the data relevant to their specific interests, avoiding the need to download the entire dataset\.### External Bioinformatics Tool Wrappers

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The AlphaFold pipeline integrates with various third\-party bioinformatics tools, such as [run\_alphafold\.py L79](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/run_alphafold.py#L79), [run\_alphafold\.py L84](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/run_alphafold.py#L84), [jackhmmer\.py L31](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L31), [hmmbuild\.py L27](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hmmbuild.py#L27), [hmmsearch\.py L29](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L29), and [kalign\.py L36](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/kalign.py#L36), to generate the essential input features for protein structure prediction\. Python wrappers are provided in [`alphafold/data/tools`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools) to manage the execution of these external tools, handle temporary files, parse their output, and streamline their integration into the overall AlphaFold workflow\.

 These wrappers abstract the complexities of subprocess execution and command\-line argument construction\. For instance, the [hhblits\.py L32](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hhblits.py#L32) class in [`alphafold/data/tools/hhblits.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hhblits.py) manages parameters like CPU count, number of iterations, and E\-value thresholds, executing the [run\_alphafold\.py L79](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/run_alphafold.py#L79) binary to perform protein sequence database searches and generate multiple sequence alignments \(MSAs\)\. Similarly, the [hhsearch\.py L29](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hhsearch.py#L29) class in [`alphafold/data/tools/hhsearch.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hhsearch.py) provides an interface for [run\_alphafold\.py L84](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/run_alphafold.py#L84) queries, parsing HHR output into structured template hit objects\.

 For profile HMM construction and searching, the [hmmbuild\.py L27](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hmmbuild.py#L27) class in [`alphafold/data/tools/hmmbuild.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hmmbuild.py) builds HMM profiles from MSAs \(either Stockholm or A3M format\), while the [hmmsearch\.py L29](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L29) class in [`alphafold/data/tools/hmmsearch.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/hmmsearch.py) then queries sequence databases with these profiles\. The [jackhmmer\.py L31](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L31) class in [`alphafold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py) wraps the [jackhmmer\.py L31](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L31) binary for homology searches, supporting both local and streamed database queries\. This streaming capability, enabled by [jackhmmer\.py L49](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L49) and [jackhmmer\.py L50](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L50), allows efficient processing of very large databases by concurrently downloading and processing data chunks\. Finally, the [kalign\.py L36](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/kalign.py#L36) class in [`alphafold/data/tools/kalign.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/kalign.py) handles multiple sequence alignments, preparing input sequences and executing the [kalign\.py L36](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/kalign.py#L36) binary\.

 Each wrapper employs [kalign\.py L90](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/kalign.py#L90) for command execution and utilizes [utils\.py L25](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/utils.py#L25) from [`alphafold/data/tools/utils.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/utils.py) to ensure robust temporary file management and cleanup\. Error handling is detailed, typically raising [prng\.py L37](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/model/prng.py#L37) with [kalign\.py L91](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/kalign.py#L91) and [kalign\.py L91](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/tools/kalign.py#L91) to provide diagnostics for tool failures\. These wrappers are crucial for automating the feature generation step, which is a prerequisite for the [AlphaFold Inference Pipeline](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-inference-pipeline)\.## AlphaFold Server Job Submission

```
{
  "name": "MyProteinFoldJob",
  "modelSeeds": [], // Empty list for automated random seed assignment
  "dialect": "alphafoldserver",
  "version": 1,
  "sequences": [
    {
      "proteinChain": {
        "sequence": "SEQUENCE", // Amino acid sequence
        "count": 1, // Number of copies of this protein chain
        "useStructureTemplate": true // Use PDB templates (default is true)
        // Other proteinChain fields can be added here, e.g., glycans, modifications, unpairedMsa
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

The AlphaFold server automates protein structure prediction tasks through a standardized JSON file format, as detailed in [`server/README.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md)\. This enables engineers to submit multiple modeling jobs with specified parameters and molecular entities, facilitating scalable and reproducible predictions\. Each job within the JSON file includes a unique [pyproject\.toml L20](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/pyproject.toml#L20), a list of [README\.md?plain=1 L31](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L31) for model initialization \(an empty list is recommended for automatic seed assignment\), and a [parsers\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/parsers.py#L33) array describing the molecules to be modeled\. The JSON structure also requires a [README\.md?plain=1 L43](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L43) field set to [README\.md?plain=1 L58](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L58) and a [pyproject\.toml L63](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/pyproject.toml#L63) field set to [LICENSE L8](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/LICENSE#L8), which supports features like [README\.md?plain=1 L70](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L70) and [README\.md?plain=1 L70](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L70)\.

 The [parsers\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/parsers.py#L33) array can define various molecular entities:

 - **Protein Chains**: These are specified with details such as the protein sequence, optional [README\.md?plain=1 L80](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L80) and [LICENSE L27](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/LICENSE#L27) \(using CCD codes\), [README\.md?plain=1 L334](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L334) for multiple copies, a boolean [README\.md?plain=1 L70](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L70) \(defaulting to [README\.md?plain=1 L376](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L376)\), a [README\.md?plain=1 L70](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L70) \(ISO 8601 format\) for template cutoff, and an optional [README\.md?plain=1 L111](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L111) in A3M format for Multiple Sequence Alignment\. Custom structural [README\.md?plain=1 L133](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L133) can also be provided as a list of dictionaries containing [README\.md?plain=1 L160](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L160) content, along with [README\.md?plain=1 L122](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L122) and [README\.md?plain=1 L124](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L124) to map residues\. For further details on how these entities are handled, see [Entity\-Specific Modeling Parameters](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-server-job-submission-entity-specific-modeling-parameters)\.
- **DNA Sequences**: These specify the single\-stranded DNA sequence \(A, T, G, C\), [README\.md?plain=1 L334](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L334), and optional [LICENSE L27](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/LICENSE#L27) \(using CCD codes\)\. Double\-stranded DNA modeling requires two [README\.md?plain=1 L53](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L53) entries for the forward and reverse complement strands\.
- **RNA Sequences**: Similar to DNA, these define single\-stranded RNA sequences \(A, U, G, C\), [README\.md?plain=1 L334](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L334), and optional [LICENSE L27](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/LICENSE#L27)\.
- **Ligands and Ions**: These are specified by their respective [README\.md?plain=1 L93](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L93) and [README\.md?plain=1 L334](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/afdb/README.md?plain=1#L334)\.

 For a comprehensive understanding of the JSON structure, including all top\-level fields and how sequences are defined, refer to [AlphaFold Server JSON Request Schema](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-server-job-submission-alphafold-server-json-request-schema)\. An initial template JSON file can be obtained by running a job via the AlphaFold Server GUI and extracting the [README\.md?plain=1 L20](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L20) file from the result zip\.### AlphaFold Server JSON Request Schema

```
[
  {
    "name": "My AlphaFold Job",
    "modelSeeds": [],
    "sequences": [
      // ... content for proteinChain, dnaSequence, rnaSequence, ligand, or ion entities
    ],
    "dialect": "alphafoldserver",
    "version": 1
  }
]
```

Job submissions to the AlphaFold Server are defined by a JSON file format, enabling the automation of modeling tasks\. This format is specified in [`server/README.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md)\. Each submission is a list of dictionaries, where each dictionary represents a distinct job\. This structure allows for multiple jobs to be batched within a single file\.

 Every job description mandates specific top\-level fields:

 - [pyproject\.toml L20](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/pyproject.toml#L20): A string identifier for the job, used in the job history\.
- [README\.md?plain=1 L31](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L31): A list of strings representing [README\.md?plain=1 L31](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L31) seed values for model initialization\. An empty list is recommended for automatic random seed assignment\.
- [parsers\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/parsers.py#L33): A list of dictionaries that detail the molecular entities \(e\.g\., proteins, DNA, RNA, ligands, ions\) to be modeled\.
- [README\.md?plain=1 L43](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L43): Must be set to [README\.md?plain=1 L58](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L58)\.
- [pyproject\.toml L63](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/pyproject.toml#L63): Set to [LICENSE L8](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/LICENSE#L8)\. This version specifically supports fields such as [README\.md?plain=1 L70](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L70) and [README\.md?plain=1 L70](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L70)\.

 The [parsers\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/parsers.py#L33) field is critical as it defines the inputs for the AlphaFold models\. It accommodates various molecular entity types, each with its own set of parameters for specifying the sequence, count, modifications, and other modeling considerations\. For example, [README\.md?plain=1 L52](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L52) entries can include details about glycans, post\-translational modifications, and even custom structural templates, as further described in [Entity\-Specific Modeling Parameters](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold#alphafold-server-job-submission-entity-specific-modeling-parameters)\.### Entity\-Specific Modeling Parameters

```
[
  {
    "name": "Multi-entity Modeling Example",
    "modelSeeds": [],
    "sequences": [
      {
        "proteinChain": {
          "sequence": "PREACHINGS",
          "count": 1,
          "glycans": [ { "residues": "NAG", "position": 1 } ]
        }
      },
      {
        "dnaSequence": {
          "sequence": "GATTACA",
          "count": 1,
          "modifications": [ { "modificationType": "CCD_6OG", "basePosition": 1 } ]
        }
      },
      {
        "ligand": {
          "ligand": "CCD_ATP",
          "count": 1
        }
      },
      {
        "ion": {
          "ion": "MG",
          "count": 2
        }
      }
    ],
    "dialect": "alphafoldserver",
    "version": 1
  }
]
```

AlphaFold Server job submissions, defined in the [pyproject\.toml L28](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/pyproject.toml#L28) file within [`server`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server), require a [parsers\.py L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/parsers.py#L33) list that details the molecular entities to be modeled\. Each entry in this list specifies the type of entity and its associated parameters\. This enables the server to handle diverse molecular inputs for structural predictions\.

 For [README\.md?plain=1 L52](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L52) entities, detailed specifications can include the primary sequence, along with optional [README\.md?plain=1 L80](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L80) \(specifying [README\.md?plain=1 L417](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/README.md?plain=1#L417) and [mmcif\_parsing\.py L64](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/mmcif_parsing.py#L64)\) and [LICENSE L27](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/LICENSE#L27) \(using [README\.md?plain=1 L92](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/server/README.md?plain=1#L92) and [mmcif\_parsing\.py L64](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/blob/c77e5d2a8961d1a353632c462914ff0a32a950f6/alphafold/data/mmcif_parsing.py#L64) based on CCD codes\)\.
